To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the two enzymes involved in phosphorylated recognition marker synthesis, namely, UDP-N-acetylglucose 1-phosphate: N-acetylglucoseamine 1-phosphotransferase and N-acetylglucomannosaminidase, are localized in a Golgi-like fraction of rat liver.
the phosphorylated recognition markers are synthesized by transfer of N-acetylglucose 1-phosphate to C6 hydroxy groups of mannose residues and subsequent hydrolysis of the diester bonds.
the phosphorylation of mannose residues is a post-translational modification that occurs in the Golgi apparatus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, processing and intracellular transport of lysosomal enzymes in rat liver.
the study of the biosynthesis of lysosomal enzymes.
a new concept of the biosynthesis of phosphorylated recognition marker in lysosomal enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the two phosphorylation steps in the synthesis of the phosphorylated recognition markers are located in the cis-Golgi compartment of the secretory pathway, and that the phosphorylated recognition marker is transferred to the mannose 6-phosphate receptor in the cis-Goli compartment.
the phosphorylation of lysosomal enzyme precursors is a Golgi function.
both the transferase and the diesterases are located in the Golgi apparatus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phosphorylation of lysosomal enzymes is a Golgi process.
lysosomal enzymes are synthesized in the rough endoplasmic reticulum and transported through Golgi apparatus to the lysosomes.
the phosphorylated recognition markers are synthesized in the Golgi apparatus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Golgi apparatus is the site of phosphorylation of lysosomal enzyme precursors.
the phosphorylation of mannose residues is not an early event during the processing of lysosomal enzymes.

the Golgi apparatus is a dynamic organelle that is constantly changing its composition and function, and that the Golgi complex is not a single organelle but a series of compartments that are connected in series.
